name: Sweet pea
grown_as: A hardy annual climbing flower grown for cutting and scent, usually a Spencer variety with large wavy petals. Colour depends on the variety, which is not known: drawn mauve-pink. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A climbing annual 1.5 to 2 m up canes or netting, the whole plant softly hairy. The stem has two narrow green wings running down it. Climbs by branched tendrils.

leaf.type: Compound: a single pair of leaflets on a winged stalk that ends in a branched tendril
leaf.outline: Each leaflet oval to elliptic, 2.5 to 6 cm
leaf.tip: Pointed or with a tiny point
leaf.veins: Three to five veins running lengthways from the base
leaf.stalk: Short and winged; at its base two narrow, pointed, half arrow-shaped stipules, much smaller than the leaflets

flower.form: A pea flower: an upright back petal (the standard), two side petals (the wings) and two lower petals joined into a boat-shaped keel between the wings, the standard large and frilly
flower.petals: Five: a large upright, broad, wavy-edged standard; two wings held forward; a small curved keel
flower.colour: Varies: white, pink, mauve, purple, crimson, often two-toned. Drawn mauve-pink.
flower.behind: A green hairy calyx with five pointed teeth
flower.carried: In sprays of 2 to 5 on long, stiff, upright stalks (15 to 30 cm) from the leaf joints, held well above the leaves

fruit: Hairy pods 5 to 7 cm, green turning pale brown; they twist open to drop round, dark brown or mottled seeds about 5 mm. The seeds are poisonous.
seedling: The seed leaves stay in the seed underground. A stem with small scale leaves comes up, then leaves of one pair of narrow leaflets with a tendril.
winter: Nothing: an annual (autumn-sown plants overwinter under cover as small plants)

leaf: a branched tendril at the tip
seedling: a thin shoot with a pair of narrow leaflets and a tendril
young: a climbing stem with paired leaflets and branched tendrils
flower: sprays of large frilly flowers on long upright stalks above the leaves
seedhead: hairy pods 5 to 7 cm, pale brown

look_alikes: Everlasting pea (Lathyrus latifolius) is a perennial with broader-winged stems, unscented magenta flowers in longer sprays and big stipules. Garden pea has huge stipules and is hairless and blue-green.
